data.narrative:
Cellino is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Nabiha Saklayen and Marinna Madrid, having raised approximately $125M to date. The valuation universe comprises 3 public comparables in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, though the private peer set lacks sufficient stage and valuation alignment for direct median benchmarking.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proves applicable. This method uses total capital raised ($125M) as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to post-Series A progression, yielding $250M. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage peer datapoints within the Biotech & Health sector—while 7 same-sector peers exist, none met clustering thresholds. Public-comp anchoring cannot be executed because Cellino's revenue is not disclosed, precluding P/S multiple application despite a median 8.1x ratio across the 3 public tickers.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $212M to $288M, centered on $250M. This range reflects sensitivity around stage-progression assumptions rather than cross-method convergence. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for Cellino's specific risk profile and capital efficiency relative to peer benchmarks, and the absence of revenue data that would enable public-comp validation.
